study: Robinson-Smith et al. (2018/2019), EasyPeasy home-learning play programme, cluster RCT, EEF, language
eval_evidence: Independent EEF evaluation: 'The project was independently evaluated by a team from Durham University and York Trials Unit, University of York' (School of Education, Durham). The intervention developer (EasyPeasy) is separate from the evaluators.
developer_evidence: The TPD element - training each nursery's 'Pod Leader' - was delivered by the developer: 'a member of nursery staff (the Pod Leader), trained by EasyPeasy' (a one-hour online webinar plus dashboard training from EasyPeasy). The developer trained the in-school coordinators directly.
cascade_evidence: EasyPeasy trained nursery Pod Leaders, who then coordinated parental engagement; the actual delivery to children ran through parents at home (and the Pod Leader is an intermediary coordinator). Transmission passes through the Pod Leader/parents rather than developer-to-classroom-teacher directly. (Non-standard TPD: largely a parent-facing programme.)
counterfactual_evidence: Two-armed trial comparing EasyPeasy to 'business as usual in control schools' (nurseries that did not receive EasyPeasy); no alternative programme for controls.
coaching_evidence: The teacher-facing component was a one-hour online webinar plus dashboard training for Pod Leaders; no ongoing in-class coaching of teachers.
student_dose_evidence: Substantial direct child-facing dose beyond regular nursery instruction: parents received weekly texts linking to 65 play-based games over 20 weeks to play with their children at home (a parent-delivered home-learning dose). Adds instruction beyond the teacher's regular classroom instruction.
maturity_evidence: EasyPeasy is a single 20-week home-learning programme delivered once (Sept 2017-summer 2018) with outcomes measured immediately after; no multi-year rollout / maturity axis.
